title: Sparsity-probing kernel selector and rolling KV-window eviction for model-specific throughput gains
author: Lydia Chen
release_notes: Introduces sparsity-aware kernel selection and rolling KV-window eviction to improve P95 latency and throughput for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants; no API changes.
body: Motivation: certain model variants (mixed-head MQA/GQA and models with intra-head sparsity patterns) do not map well to our default kernel dispatch and KV retention policies. This leads to suboptimal kernel paths and premature KV eviction under bursty, low-latency workloads. Summary: implement a sparsity-probing kernel selector and a rolling KV-window eviction strategy that adapts retention to observed attention-density patterns per-request and per-model. The new selector probes a small representative head-slice at runtime to pick a kernel variant (dense / sparse-optimized / hybrid) and caches the choice keyed by model+seq_profile. The rolling KV-window keeps a sliding retention budget (ms-based) instead of a fixed token count, allowing high-density bursts to preserve KV while low-density requests compact more aggressively. Key changes: - runtime/kernel_selector.rs: new KernelProbe + selection cache - runtime/kv_window.rs: rolling window state machine, eviction policy, and metrics - runtime/scheduler_continuous_batching.rs: small smoothing update to avoid microburst thrashing - perf tests and regression benchmarks added under tests/perf - docs/perf/kernel-selection.md: rationale and tuning knobs - examples/bench-configs/microbatch.toml: sample params Safety & rollout: feature gated behind env var REDWOOD_RUNTIME_SPARSE_PROBE and disabled by default for Dedicated/Private until opt-in. Gradual rollout: enable in perf canary -> 10% region -> full. Local snippet (runtime kernel probe): "let probe = SampleHeads::new(4); let variant = probe.select(&attn_stats); cache.insert(model_id, variant);" Benchmarks (internal): - Llama-2-13B (MQA) @ 1024 seq: P95 latency down 9%, throughput +12% under mixed short/long workload - Mistral-7B (GQA) @ 512 seq: throughput +14% in continuous-batching mode - Qwen-7B variants: tail latency improved 6% and tokens saved ~3% by avoiding unnecessary kernel fallbacks Known limitations: kernel probe adds ~0.5ms overhead on first-seen model+profile but is amortized across sessions. The rolling window currently uses wall-clock ms which may skew under host clock drift; we instrumented for this and plan to switch to monotonic time in follow-up. Related work: ENG-1984 (kernel dispatch refactor), ENG-2003 (kv retention study). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for eviction invariants - [x] Perf harness added - [x] Docs and knobs - [x] Canary rollout plan

notes: This PR targets model-specific runtime optimization space: it is intentionally conservative in default behavior but provides knobs to unlock higher throughput for teams willing to opt in.
Follow-ups planned: monotonic time swap, adaptive probe sample size, expose admin endpoint to evict KV per-session.
